A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LoongX and L-Mind. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison, including matching material moved within v3.pdf.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original image-editing evaluations, architecture and modality ablations, editing-type classification experiments, and participant-level results.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains those original results and adds evaluations involving five previously unseen participants in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The main CS3/DGF architecture, objectives, and DiT update remain unchanged. New Appendix D.2 describes deterministic flow-aware inversion with a rank-128 LoRA velocity-to-score bridge. Because v2 already uses LoRA and v3 presents this as supplementary derivation, the PDFs do not establish whether it changes the implemented procedure or documents an existing component.

E1.justification: Appendix E.1 extends evaluation from the original young-adult cohort to five unseen participants aged 13–63, adding cross-user and broader age coverage. The original L-Mind dataset, editing categories, and input modalities remain.

E2.justification: OminiControl with text and speech remains the evaluated comparator set. Table 5 extends these same comparators to unseen participants; its spelling 'OmniControl' does not identify a different method. Newly cited editing methods are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added cross-subject protocol explicitly excludes five participants from training, with 500, 500, 200, 100, and 100 samples reported respectively. Existing splits, metrics, and inference settings remain. Appendix C also introduces eight-channel sensor descriptions differing from retained main-text counts, without establishing that acquisition settings changed.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 adds a targeted cross-subject generalization analysis addressing possible participant overlap in the original evaluation. Existing modality, channel, architecture, and sequence-length analyses remain. Tables 6–7 tabulate existing plots, and the new 'More Failure Cases' subsection repeats the existing Figure 14 cases.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain identical means and 95% confidence intervals over three runs. The added cross-subject results introduce no documented run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original participant rows remain numerically unchanged. Tables 4–5 add unseen-participant results: neural-only LoongX obtains CLIP-I 0.6019 and DINO 0.4037, versus the text baseline's 0.6528 and 0.4655 on that test set. These are additional results under different participant conditions, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a localized mathematical treatment of stochastic diffusion, probability-flow inversion, stochastic–deterministic interpolation, and a velocity-to-score mapping. The existing main-method equations remain unchanged; the expanded Beer–Lambert equations restate previously supplied mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: L-Mind, LoongX with CS3/DGF, and complementary neural and speech conditioning. Headline performance claims and proposed VR/XR applications retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The appendices substantially expand applicability and mechanism interpretations, including transferable representations across unseen users, avoiding motor-calibration requirements, and rationales for pairing modalities with T5 versus CLIP. Section 5.6 adds a spatial-editing limitation. The new strong-generalization interpretation exceeds Table 5's support because neural-only CLIP-I and DINO no longer surpass the text baseline.

D1.justification: v3 reports code and dataset release instead of a future release promise, and substantially expands acquisition, preprocessing, and inversion documentation, including optical sampling rates and LoRA rank. It also identifies an fNIRS pretraining source and names the approving institution. Some sensor descriptions remain unreconciled, and the explicit AdamW optimizer name disappears. Actual online availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: New Appendix B substantially broadens the literature discussion across BCI, brain-supervised generation, multimodal learning, and future research. Additional positioning connects the work to DreamConnect, world models, and diffusion-inversion methods such as SDEdit and LEDITS++. Existing core novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The single technical appendix is reorganized into Appendices A–E, with substantial explanatory expansion and redistribution of subject information, limitations, and experiments. Experimental setup moves into main-text Section 5.1, discussion paragraphs are rewritten, and authorship, affiliations, acknowledgments, and publication header are updated.

P2.justification: All fourteen figure assets are retained unchanged, although several move and captions receive edits. Table 4 gains unseen-participant rows; Table 5 adds the cross-subject comparison; Tables 6–7 provide tabular displays of existing ablation plots. The overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The unseen-participant evaluation partially addresses v2's acknowledged generalization gap, while explicit ablation tables and expanded technical documentation make the work easier to assess. These are useful, limited gains. Their value is tempered by the overly strong interpretation of Table 5 and unreconciled sensor descriptions; the original benchmark results remain unchanged.
